channel.title: The Trading Journal
channel.description: A daily log of trades, lessons, and probabilities

item.title: Adjustment Rules — When to Roll, When to Hedge, When to Hold
item.description: The judgment framework for managing open positions: when to roll a spread, when to hedge with a long option, when to hold through volatility, and when to accept the loss and move on.

item.title: Correlation and Portfolio Construction
item.description: How correlated positions affect total portfolio risk, the difference between name-level and market-level correlation, and the journal's rules for basket exposure and concentration limits.

item.title: Debit Vertical Spread — The Defined-Risk Directional
item.description: Anatomy of a debit vertical spread: lower max-loss than a long call, capped upside, and the trade-off between risk reduction and profit potential. When the spread fits a directional thesis better than a single-leg long option.

item.title: Diagonal Spread — The Time-Distributed Position
item.description: Anatomy of a diagonal spread: long option at a longer expiration, short option at a shorter expiration, the structure's time-distributed payoff, and when the diagonal fits better than a vertical or a calendar.

item.title: Edge Sources — Where the Journal's Returns Come From
item.description: The structural, statistical, and informational edges that the journal's playbook exploits — why each exists, how the journal identifies them, and how the edge degrades over time.

item.title: Exit Discipline — The Hardest Part of the Trade
item.description: The discipline of closing positions at the right time: the take-profit rule, the stop-loss rule, the early-close rules, and the most common reasons traders exit too early or too late.

item.title: Expected Value — The Math Behind Every Trade
item.description: The expected value formula for options trades, how the journal calculates probability of profit, the difference between theoretical and realized expected value, and why a positive EV is necessary but not sufficient.

item.title: The Greeks — Delta, Gamma, Theta, Vega, Rho
item.description: The five option greeks: delta, gamma, theta, vega, rho — what each measures, how they interact in a position, and the greeks the journal monitors at entry and during the life of the position.

item.title: Implied Volatility — The Price of Optionality
item.description: What implied volatility is, how it differs from realized volatility, why the option's price is dominated by IV rather than the underlying's expected move, and how the journal uses IV rank to choose structures.

item.title: Iron Butterfly — The High-Probability Mean-Reversion
item.description: Anatomy of an iron butterfly: short straddle with protective wings, very high probability of profit, defined risk, and the trade-off between premium collected and the cost of being wrong. When the structure fits a low-volatility regime better than an iron condor.

item.title: Journal Discipline — The Process Audit
item.description: How the journal audits its own process: position-level review, weekly recap, monthly methodology audit, and the role of the trade log in catching pattern errors before they cost the book.

item.title: Journaling Cadence — Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly
item.description: The four cadences of the journal's process discipline: the daily note, the weekly recap, the monthly methodology audit, and the quarterly strategic review. The four together produce the playbook's living-document quality.

item.title: Options Market Microstructure — How the Bid/Ask and the Open Interest Shape the Trade
item.description: The microstructure of the options market: bid/ask spreads, open interest, volume, and the way the interaction of the order book shapes the journal's entry and exit prices. The hidden cost of every trade that the price doesn't show.

item.title: Options vs. Equity Trading — Why the Journal Focuses on Options
item.description: The structural differences between options trading and equity trading: leverage, time decay, defined risk, and the ways the differences shape the journal's methodology. Why the journal focuses on options and how the focus changes the strategy.

item.title: Position Sizing — The Fixed-Fractional Method
item.description: How the journal sizes every position: fixed-fractional risk per trade, max-loss cap per position, and the relationship between NLV, leverage, and structure choice.

item.title: Reading the Trade Log — How to Evaluate the Journal's Methodology
item.description: How to read the trade log: filtering by structure, by ticker, by outcome; the difference between hit rate and expected value; and the patterns to look for when evaluating the journal's methodology.

item.title: Risk Management — The Framework That Keeps the Journal in the Game
item.description: The journal's risk management framework: position-level risk, portfolio-level risk, drawdown limits, and the difference between acceptable and unacceptable loss. The rules that the journal will not break even when the playbook says it should.

item.title: Rules vs. Discretion — Where the Journal Lets the Trader Decide
item.description: The line between mechanical rules and discretionary judgment in the playbook: which decisions are rule-based, which are discretionary, and why the journal keeps the discretionary set as small as possible.

item.title: Statistical Foundation — Why the Math Works
item.description: The statistical foundation of the journal's methodology: the normal distribution, the central limit theorem, the law of large numbers, and how each applies to the realized outcomes of the playbook's structures.

item.title: Trade Entries — The Anatomy of a Trade Log Record
item.description: The standard format for every trade log entry: instrument, structure, strikes, expiration, premium, target, stop, reasoning, and the expected value calculation that justifies the position.
